findings.title: Ordinary object matching loses word-prefix matches
findings.evidence: paired TCP execution + C/Rust source tracing + Rust characterization
findings.setup: Create a carried thing named Red Sword; use look sword.
findings.c_result: Red Sword is selected and described.
findings.effect: Valid abbreviations for later words fail. The shared matcher also serves inventory operations; the paired probe exercises look.
findings.recommendation: Use the C word-prefix matcher consistently for ordinary local candidates; keep exact-match precedence, lock preferences and scope.
findings.resolution: Resolved using the existing C word-prefix helper in the shared ordinary matcher. Original C/Rust results above and behavioral-wire.json remain historical. Positive ordinary-matching, scope, ambiguity, type/MATCH-lock, possessive/inventory and TCP restart regressions cover the correction.

findings.title: Fallback description content loses precedence over its provider
findings.evidence: paired TCP execution + C/Rust source tracing + Rust characterization
findings.setup: Give Red Sword stored description STORED DESCRIPTION and audit.lua messages.describe returning PROVIDER DESCRIPTION while setting audit.provider=true.
findings.c_result: STORED DESCRIPTION; provider still executes and sets state.
findings.rust_result: PROVIDER DESCRIPTION; provider executes and sets state.
findings.effect: Stored descriptions become invisible whenever a describe provider supplies direct text, even though C gives stored content priority.
findings.recommendation: Model stored description/internal-description priority explicitly after provider evaluation. Do not skip provider mutations or on_describe.
findings.resolution: Resolved: live stored content is selected after provider execution; room appearance is internal, including transparent-exit views. Historical results above are preserved. Positive Rust and TCP regressions cover the correction.

findings.title: Transparent exit selects the remote room external renderer
findings.evidence: paired TCP execution + C/Rust source tracing + Rust characterization
findings.setup: Link a transparent exit to a room with distinct INTERNAL ROOM VIEW and EXTERNAL ROOM VIEW callbacks; look at the exit from its source.
findings.effect: Copied room modules commonly supply only internal_appearance; remote room views fall back or lose their intended rendering.
findings.recommendation: Select internal appearance for rooms regardless of viewer location, retaining the approved container distinction and transaction staging.
findings.resolution: Resolved: live stored content is selected after provider execution; room appearance is internal, including transparent-exit views. Historical results above are preserved. Positive Rust and TCP regressions cover the correction.

findings.title: Private pages reach contained non-recipients
findings.evidence: paired TCP execution + C/Rust source tracing + Rust characterization
findings.setup: Connect GOD and Wizard, teleport Wizard inside GOD, then GOD pages GOD with PRIVATE-PAGE.
findings.c_result: Only GOD receives the page and sender confirmation; Wizard receives no text.
findings.rust_result: Wizard also receives GOD pages: PRIVATE-PAGE, despite last-page recipients containing only GOD.
findings.effect: A player inside another player receives private communications without being named as a recipient. This is recipient expansion, not a multiple-session difference.
findings.recommendation: Fix page delivery first. Match the C direct-player notification policy; audit related channel/non-player delivery separately rather than globally disabling legitimate broadcasts.
findings.resolution: Resolved by direct player notification. Original results above remain historical; behavioral-wire-d09-resolved.json records the corrected paired run.

findings.title: Mixed valid/unknown page recipients lose group annotation
findings.evidence: paired TCP execution + C/Rust source tracing + Rust characterization
findings.setup: Connect Wizard and page Wizard MissingPlayer=hello.
findings.c_result: Wizard receives To (Wizard), GOD pages you: hello. Sender reports the missing name.
findings.rust_result: Wizard receives GOD pages: hello. Sender reports the same missing name.
findings.effect: The recipient cannot see the original multi-target context. Delivery and successful-recipient history are otherwise correct in this case.
findings.recommendation: Preserve C target-token/group semantics separately from the resolved/delivered list. Review partial/offline and repeated recipients together.
findings.resolution: Recipient formatting tracks the original group request independently of successful resolution; whole names remain single-target. Sender confirmations and history remain unchanged. Original results above remain historical; behavioral-wire-d10-d11-resolved.json records corrected paired execution.

findings.title: Printable-ASCII predicate silently coerces numeric input
findings.evidence: paired TCP execution + C/Rust source tracing + Rust characterization
findings.setup: Evaluate pcall(mux.text.is_printable_ascii,123), plus ASCII and newline-containing string controls.
findings.c_result: The number is rejected; strings are accepted and return true/false as appropriate.
findings.rust_result: The number is accepted and returns true; string controls match C.
findings.effect: Callers that depend on argument validation receive a successful boolean instead of a type error. This is looser validation, not the approved stricter-input behavior.
findings.recommendation: Require an actual Lua string for this predicate, preserving binary-safe checks and documenting its argument error.
findings.resolution: Only actual Lua strings are accepted; all 256 byte values are checked directly, including binary strings. Original results above remain historical; behavioral-wire-d10-d11-resolved.json records corrected paired execution.

findings.title: Plain goto and configured movement aliases do not work
findings.evidence: paired TCP execution + C/Rust source tracing + Rust characterization
findings.setup: Create a linked exit audit-window; execute goto audit-window. The bare exit name is a working control.
findings.c_result: The caller traverses the exit and sees INTERNAL ROOM VIEW.
findings.rust_result: Unknown-command response; location does not change. Rust tests also reproduce go and move aliases.
findings.effect: Existing help and aliases advertise an unavailable core movement command. Only goto/quiet was intentionally excluded, not plain goto.
findings.recommendation: Register plain goto using the shared exit path and its access policy; retain rejection of /quiet and test native/alias/forced execution.
findings.resolution: Registered plain goto with shared local exit travel and effective access gating; positive alias, denial, queued/TCP rollback and restart regressions. Historical results above remain unchanged.
